patients.summary: Retired math teacher with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and BPH who joins in 2021. Recurrent urinary retention after a hernia repair, a knee replacement and on its own, orthostatic hypotension on tamsulosin, hyperkalemia on sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim with lisinopril, and a UTI-related delirium admission in 2025. Outside records reach the practice unevenly.

documents.body: Mr. Bennett phoned. Retired, lives in Belchertown, wants to transfer primary care here from the office he has used for years; a neighbor is a member. Explained membership, he signed up over the phone. New patient visit booked for next Tuesday morning, 60 min. Asked him to bring all his pill bottles and any recent lab printouts. Records release form emailed to edward.bennett@example.test.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT
69 y/o retired high school math teacher transferring care. Married, lives with his wife in Belchertown.

DIABETES: type 2 for many years, metformin 1000 twice a day, tolerates it. Checks sugars a few mornings a week, usually 120s-140s. No lows. No numbness or foot sores. Eye exam yearly with his optometrist.
HYPERTENSION: lisinopril 10 daily, home cuff runs low 130s.
STATIN: atorvastatin 20, started by his old PCP for the diabetes. No muscle aches.
RIGHT KNEE: arthritis, sees an outside orthopedic group, walks most days, says the knee is 'manageable for now.'
GU: no urinary complaints today.

PMH: as above. PSH: none.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: none known to medications.
FH: father type 2 diabetes, died of prostate cancer at 75. Mother hypertension. Older brother has an enlarged prostate.
SH: never smoker. A beer or a glass of wine once or twice a week. Retired from teaching math.

ROS: negative except knee as above.
EXAM: well appearing. BP and HR per flowsheet. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, nontender. Feet: skin intact, DP pulses 2+, monofilament normal both feet. Right knee crepitus, no effusion.

A/P
1. T2DM: continue metformin. A1c, CMP, urine albumin today.
2. HTN: at goal, continue lisinopril.
3. Statin: continue atorvastatin 20, lipids today.
4. R knee OA: per ortho.
5. Health maintenance: will get old records (colonoscopy, vaccines). Hep C screen today. PHQ-2 negative.
Follow up after the records come in; AWV in the fall.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Edward, your bloodwork is back. A1c is right where we want it for you, kidney function and potassium are normal, cholesterol is in a good range on the atorvastatin, and the urine protein test is normal. Hepatitis C screen negative. No changes. I'll see you in the fall for your wellness visit.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you, good to hear. My old office never explained the numbers this clearly. Ed

documents.title: Same-Day Visit: Dysuria
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted this morning, seen same day.
S: 2 days of burning when he urinates and going more often. No fever or chills, no flank pain, no blood he has noticed. First time for this. No discharge.
O: afebrile, vitals per flowsheet. Abdomen soft, mild suprapubic discomfort to palpation, no CVA tenderness.
UA dip: LE 2+, nitrite positive.
A/P: cystitis in a man, so treating as a complicated UTI. Culture sent. Cephalexin 500 four times daily x7 days. Fluids. Call if fever, back pain, or not improving in 48 h. We'll call with the culture.

conditions.label: Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/20/2022
Referred by primary care for voiding symptoms.

Mr. Bennett is a 70-year-old man with roughly half a year of daytime frequency, getting up at night to void, a slow start and a weakened stream. Urination is painless. One treated UTI in November. Started tamsulosin 0.4 mg in February through his PCP with modest effect so far.
PMH: type 2 diabetes, hypertension (well controlled), right knee osteoarthritis.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father died of prostate cancer at age 75. Brother with BPH.
Social: never smoker, social alcohol.

Exam: BP 135/85, HR 78, BMI 29. Abdomen soft, bladder not palpable. Normal phallus and testes. DRE: prostate enlarged symmetrically, firm texture, no nodules, nontender.
UA: no evidence of infection, no hematuria.
Labs (drawn today): creatinine 1.0, fasting glucose 140, PSA 2.8 ng/mL.

Impression: benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms. PSA within the age-adjusted range and exam benign; reassuring despite his father's history.
Plan: continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. Reviewed behavioral measures. Return in 6 months with post-void residual.

Thank you for this referral.
Urology

UROLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 10/10/2022

Returns 6 months after his first evaluation for BPH. Over the past half year he describes frequency, urgency and nocturia and feels he does not empty completely. Two urinary infections in the last 12 months, both treated with antibiotics by primary care.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: abdomen soft and nontender. DRE: symmetrically enlarged, firm, nontender gland, no nodules.
Urinalysis: no evidence of active infection.
Labs: creatinine 1.2, BUN 18.
Bladder ultrasound post-void residual: 120 mL.

Assessment: BPH with LUTS and an incomplete-emptying component; recurrent UTIs.
Plan: continue tamsulosin. Double voiding. Follow up as needed.

Urology

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 10/11/2023 18:50

CC: no urine output for about 8 hours with severe low abdominal pain.
HPI: 71M with BPH, seen by urology in April and October of last year, who had an elective inguinal hernia repair two days ago. Over the past year he has had progressive trouble voiding: weak stream, nighttime voiding, a feeling of not emptying. Since this morning he has not been able to pass urine at all and the lower belly pain is now severe.
PMH: BPH, type 2 diabetes, hypertension. Recent right inguinal herniorrhaphy (10/09).
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide, metformin, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, social drinker.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 88. Uncomfortable, shifting on the stretcher. Abdomen distended with suprapubic tenderness. Right groin incision clean and dry. DRE: enlarged firm prostate, not tender.
Bedside bladder ultrasound: markedly distended bladder, estimated 600 mL.

Course: urethral catheter placed without difficulty with prompt relief.
Impression: acute urinary retention after hernia repair, underlying BPH.
Disposition: home with indwelling catheter and leg bag; continue tamsulosin; urology office for voiding trial in about one week. Return for fever, catheter blockage or bleeding.

Record received by fax 10/13/2023.

documents.title: ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I ended up in the ER last night. Couldn't pee at all after the hernia surgery. They put a catheter in and I have to keep it until urology sees me next Wednesday. Feeling much better, just a nuisance.

documents.title: RE: ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry to hear it, but glad you got relief. That happens sometimes after surgery when the prostate is already enlarged. Keep the bag below your bladder, drink normally, and call us for fever, chills, or if it stops draining. Let me know how the urology visit goes.

documents.title: Catheter out
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Urology took the catheter out yesterday and I passed their test, peed on my own before I left. Back to normal.

documents.title: RE: Catheter out
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Great news, thanks for the update. We'll add a note to your chart. We haven't received anything from urology about yesterday; if they gave you paperwork, you can send us a photo.

2. T2DM: A1c 7.2, continue metformin.
3. HTN: continue lisinopril.

Call if a fall or fainting. Follow up in the spring.

documents.title: Preoperative Medical Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP EVALUATION
Procedure: right total knee arthroplasty, outside orthopedics, planned 4/22/2024.
Functional capacity: walks 1-2 miles, climbs two flights without chest pain or dyspnea (limited by knee, not breath). No cardiac history.
Problems: T2DM on metformin; HTN on lisinopril; BPH on tamsulosin with acute retention after hernia repair in Oct 2023; orthostatic hypotension on standing (counseled Dec, now taking tamsulosin at night, fewer spells). Hernia repaired in October, problem list updated.
Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Right knee crepitus, varus.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm.
Labs today: CBC, BMP, A1c.
Assessment: acceptable risk for planned orthopedic surgery.
Recommendations to the surgical team:
- Hold metformin the morning of surgery; resume when eating.
- Hold lisinopril the morning of surgery.
- Continue tamsulosin, including the night before. History of postoperative urinary retention: please monitor voiding before discharge.
- Get up slowly with PT given orthostatic symptoms.
Form completed and faxed with ECG and labs once resulted.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE
Date of service 04/23/2024, arrival 03:10

Chief complaint: lower abdominal pain, cannot urinate.
HPI: 72-year-old man with recurrent BPH and a prior episode of acute urinary retention in October 2023, who had a right total knee replacement about 18 hours ago and went home the same day. Has not been able to void since the surgery; lower abdominal discomfort building through the night.
PMH: BPH, urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension, type 2 diabetes, hypertension. Right TKA 04/22/2024.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 165/90, HR 102. In obvious distress. Abdomen distended and tender over the suprapubic area. Right knee dressing clean, dry, intact.
Urethral catheterization attempted by nursing, unable to pass.
Portable bladder ultrasound: approximately 750 mL.

Course: urology on call came in and placed a coude catheter with return of urine and relief of pain. Heart rate and pressure settled.
Impression: acute urinary retention after total knee arthroplasty, BPH.
Disposition: discharged with indwelling catheter, continue tamsulosin, urology clinic voiding trial in one week.

Faxed to PCP 04/26/2024.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED PROVIDER NOTE
Visit 10/14/2024

Chief complaint: severe lower abdominal pain, unable to pass urine for 24 hours.
HPI: Third presentation for retention. Over the last six months he has had increasing difficulty starting his stream, a weak stream, and getting up at night. For the past day he has passed essentially nothing and now has severe suprapubic pain.
PMH: BPH, urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, s/p right TKA.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: abdomen distended, tender suprapubically. DRE: enlarged, firm, nontender prostate.
Labs: creatinine 1.2, BUN 18.
Bladder scan: 300 mL.

Course: catheter placed, urine drained with relief.
Assessment: recurrent urinary retention, BPH.
Plan: home with catheter; urology for voiding trial.

Copy sent to primary care 11/20/2024 on request.

documents.title: ED Visit Report
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called: in the ER yesterday morning, couldn't urinate for a whole day, catheter placed again. Urology voiding trial set for next Monday. No fever, draining clear. Booked to see PCP next Tuesday. Asked ER for the record.

The ED record has not come yet; he says his kidney numbers were 'ok.'

documents.title: Follow-up Visit: Fatigue, Hyperkalemia
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Scheduled chronic care visit (diabetes, HTN, BPH with past retention).
He feels basically ok but for about two weeks has been more tired than usual and his legs and arms feel weak, e.g. carrying groceries in. Denies chest pain, palpitations, fainting.
New info: went to an urgent care Monday 4/14 for burning and frequency, was given sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim DS twice daily for 7 days. Takes the last tablet tonight. We did not get a note from the urgent care; pharmacy fill history confirms the script. Urinary symptoms gone.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10 daily, tamsulosin 0.4 qHS, atorvastatin 20, SMX-TMP as above.

Pre-visit labs Friday: K 5.8 (high), creatinine 1.4 (his usual is 1.0), BUN 18, Na 140, glucose 160.

Exam: BP 135/85. Exam unremarkable: heart regular, lungs clear, strength full on testing, reflexes normal, no edema.
ECG in office: NSR, no peaked T waves.

A/P
1. Hyperkalemia with a creatinine bump, most likely trimethoprim on top of lisinopril. ECG reassuring. Finish tonight's dose and stop; no refill. Avoid potassium supplements, salt substitutes, NSAIDs. Repeat BMP in 1 week. Lisinopril continued for now.
2. Fatigue and weakness: likely related to #1; reassess with the repeat labs.
3. UTI treated at urgent care, symptoms resolved.
4. T2DM, HTN, BPH: no other changes.

documents.title: Repeat BMP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium back to 4.7 and creatinine 1.1 off the antibiotic. Hyperkalemia resolved. Messaged pt. If he needs an antibiotic for a urinary infection in the future, avoid trimethoprim while on lisinopril; added to the chart alert.

documents.title: Your repeat labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, your potassium and kidney numbers are back to normal. It was the antibiotic interacting with your blood pressure pill. Energy should come back over the next week or so. If you ever get another bladder infection, please call us first so we can pick a different antibiotic.

documents.title: RE: Your repeat labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Already feeling stronger. Lesson learned, I'll call you first next time.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Arrival 10/16/2025 20:30, brought by his wife.

CC: confusion, agitation, seeing things for 2 days.
HPI: History from wife. Patient with BPH and prior urinary retention. For two days he has become steadily more muddled and restless, and at night he has been seeing people in the room who are not there. Baseline he is fully independent and sharp.
PMH: BPH, urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension, hyperkalemia (April), type 2 diabetes, hypertension, s/p right TKA.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin; tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: T 37.8 C, BP 160/90, HR 102, RR 18.
Exam: not oriented to time or place; attention waxes and wanes. Mild tenderness above the pubis. Otherwise no focal findings; neck supple, lungs clear, heart regular.
Labs: Na 140, K 4.2, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.2, glucose 180. WBC 9.0, Hgb 13.5. UA: leukocyte esterase and nitrite positive. Urine culture sent.
Impression: delirium due to urinary tract infection.
Plan: ceftriaxone IV, admit to medicine.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/16/2025, discharged 10/19/2025.
Principal diagnosis: delirium due to medical condition (urinary tract infection).
Secondary: UTI; BPH with history of retention; type 2 diabetes; hypertension; orthostatic hypotension.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED with two days of confusion and nocturnal visual hallucinations. Started on IV ceftriaxone. Urine culture grew E. coli, susceptible to ceftriaxone and cephalexin. Delirium precautions: lights on by day, glasses, wife at bedside, sleep protected. Mental status improved steadily and by hospital day 3 he was oriented, conversant and back to baseline per his wife. No antipsychotics required. Ambulating independently.

Discharge medications: cephalexin 500 mg four times daily to complete 10 days total antibiotic therapy; metformin 1000 mg BID; lisinopril 10 mg daily; tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: primary care within 1 week.

Hospital medicine

documents.title: Wife Calling: Admission
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called. She took him to the ER last night; for two days he'd been confused and agitated and seeing things at night. They found a urine infection and admitted him. He is calmer this morning on IV antibiotics. She will call when discharge is planned. PCP notified. Will book post-discharge visit.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Interactive contact within 2 business days of discharge. Home since yesterday noon. Wife says he's himself again, sleeping normally. Taking cephalexin four times a day, plus his usual meds. Voiding ok. Visit booked Friday 10/24. We have no discharge paperwork yet; she'll bring the copy they gave her.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospitalized 10/16-10/19 with delirium from an E. coli UTI (per the discharge medication sheet his wife brought; full summary not yet received). IV ceftriaxone, then cephalexin to finish 10 days, last dose Sunday.
Today: alert, oriented, joking. Wife agrees he is back to baseline. No dysuria, no fever. Voiding with his usual slow stream; no retention.
Med reconciliation: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4 qHS, atorvastatin 20, cephalexin (short course). No trimethoprim, good.
Exam: afebrile, vitals per flowsheet. Oriented x3, attention normal. Abdomen soft, nontender. Heart regular, lungs clear.
A/P
1. Delirium due to UTI: resolved.
2. UTI: finishing cephalexin, symptoms gone; will close after the course.
3. BPH with recurrent retention: no retention this time. Urology follow-up still not done; strongly encouraged.
4. Return precautions for confusion or fever given to wife.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit and Chronic Care
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV + follow-up, 74M.
Function: independent, drives, walks daily. No falls; stands up in stages. Brief cognitive screen normal, no lingering effects from the October delirium per wife. PHQ-2 0.
GU: since 2023 he has had three episodes of acute retention (after hernia repair, after knee replacement, then spontaneous in Oct 2024) and an E. coli UTI that made him delirious last fall, all on tamsulosin alone. Beyond the catheter checks he has not had a urology visit since 2022. Talked plainly about why it's time to look at longer-term options; he agrees to go.
DM, HTN, statin: as before, labs today.
Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft, no bladder palpable. Feet: intact sensation, pulses present.
A/P
1. BPH with recurrent urinary retention: referral to urology to discuss definitive treatment. Continue tamsulosin.
2. Orthostatic hypotension: same precautions.
3. T2DM: A1c, CMP, urine albumin today. Continue metformin.
4. HTN: continue lisinopril 10.
5. Atorvastatin 20, lipids today.
6. Prevention: flu and COVID in the fall; colonoscopy due 2027 per 2017 report, will discuss whether to continue at that point.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.body: Hi Edward, your labs from Friday are fine: A1c steady, kidney function and potassium normal, cholesterol on target, urine protein normal. The urology office should be contacting you; if you don't hear in two weeks, call them or let us know.
